newsitem.title: BELGIUM: COCKERILL SAYS FUTURE ALLIANCE POSSIBLE.
newsitem.headline: COCKERILL SAYS FUTURE ALLIANCE POSSIBLE.

text.p: Belgian steel group Cockerill Sambre reiterated on Wednesday that an alliance with another group was a possibility for the long term.
"I've always said that in time Cockerill Sambre could have an alliance," chairman Jean Gandois told a news conference on 1996 earnings.
However he said Cockerill would have to become more competitive before he would enter into any partnership negotiations.

Asked whether he feared Cockerill would be left isolated after the merger of the steel divisions of German industry giants Krupp and Thyssen , he said: "I don't fear isolation. I'm ready to negotiate (for a partner) when it appears necessary."
This could be "sooner than previously thought".
"I think there are some people who would be interested but I want to have made progress on Cockerill's Horizon 2000 (restructuring) plan first," he added.
Gandois hoped that all the 2,000 job losses planned under the Horizon 2000 project could be completed by the end of 1998.
However he noted trade unions had to be consulted.
He said it was possible the group could make a "slight profit" in 1997.
"In 1998 we should have a much more profitable year because of the Horizon 2000 plan," Ganddois added.
1997 steel volumes would be higher than those of 1996 in terms of tonnage.
But on average 1997 steel sales prices would be slightly lower than in 1996, partly because the company was locked into some contracts which had been made when prices were less favourable.
